cues.text: The Death of Pope Francis
Pope Francis died in Vatican City on April 21, 2025, Easter Monday, after a twelve-year pontificate marked by mercy and care for the environment.
His pontificate also emphasized attention to the peripheries of both Church and society.
His death came only a day after he made a final public appearance to bless crowds gathered in St. Peter's Square for Easter.
This opened a conclave that drew international attention to an unusually prominent candidate few had expected to see seriously considered only years before.
A Missionary from Chicago
Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost , born in Chicago on September 14, 1955, to a family of French, Italian, and Spanish descent, entered the Augustinian order in 1977 and was ordained a priest in 1982.
He spent much of his priestly ministry as a missionary in Peru , where he later served as Bishop of Chiclayo.
He became a naturalized Peruvian citizen in 2015—a genuinely dual formation, American by birth and Latin American by decades of pastoral service, that shaped his own approach to Church governance.
Before his appointment to Chiclayo, Prevost had already spent two terms as Prior General of the Augustinian order, from 2001 to 2013.
This gave him substantial experience in religious governance across the order's many provinces worldwide, well before Francis called him to Rome.
Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops
In January 2023, Pope Francis brought Prevost to Rome to serve as Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops , one of the Roman Curia's most consequential offices.
Responsible for vetting episcopal nominations across the entire world, the office gave Prevost broad, direct familiarity with the Church's global episcopate.
Francis also created him a cardinal later that same year, heading into the conclave that would follow Francis's death barely two years later.
The First American Pope
The conclave convened in early May 2025.
On May 8 , its second day of voting, the assembled cardinals elected Prevost as the 267th successor of St. Peter.
He became the first pope in the Church's two-thousand-year history to hold United States citizenship.

His years of ministry and citizenship in Peru meant the election was received, in much of Latin America, as a continuation of the Church's turn toward the Americas that Francis's own election in 2013 had begun.
Taking the Name Leo XIV
Prevost took the name Leo XIV , a choice widely understood as a deliberate homage to Pope Leo XIII, the great nineteenth-century pope of Rerum Novarum .

Leo XIII's encyclical was the founding document of modern Catholic social teaching—a signal, many commentators suggested, of the new pope's own priorities regarding labor, human dignity, and the Church's engagement with a rapidly changing economic and technological world.
Appearing on the loggia of St. Peter's Basilica, Leo XIV greeted the assembled crowd with the words "Peace be with you," before delivering his first blessing as pope.
Legacy
In the opening period of his pontificate, Leo XIV addressed the rights of migrants, environmental protection, and the rise of artificial intelligence.
He also addressed continued divisions within the Church between more traditional and more progressive currents, in ways many observers read as continuous with his predecessor’s priorities.
At the same time, many observers saw his approach as carrying his own distinct emphasis and voice.
His election remains, as of this writing, a recent and still-unfolding chapter in the Church's history, one whose fuller significance will only become clearer as his pontificate continues to develop.
